name: get_engine_info
description: Returns the engine's version, platform, launch settings and package status. Call it first, to check that the engine is new enough and to see which toolchain packages are installed. It is fast and local: it never uses the network. Missing packages are installed automatically by the tools that need them, unless auto_install is off.

inputSchema.description: The get_engine_info tool takes no inputs.
inputSchema.title: GetEngineInfoInput

PackageInfo.description: A toolchain package and whether it's installed.

bin_folder.description:
The folder with the package's programs, as an absolute path, when
the package is installed. For hosts that run one of its programs
directly, such as Verible's language server verible-verilog-ls from
the verible package. Omitted when the package isn't installed.

name.description: The package name, such as oss-cad-suite.

version.description: The package release, as a date tag (yyyy-mm-dd).

PackageStatus.description: Whether a package is ready to use.

oneOf.description:
Installed but incomplete or damaged. It is repaired when a tool needs
it, unless auto-install is off.

outputSchema.description: The engine's version, platform, launch settings and package status.

auto_install.description:
Whether the engine installs and repairs packages automatically when a
tool needs them. On by default. The host turns it off with the
--no-auto-install command-line argument.

command_line.description: The command-line arguments the engine was launched with, as given.

engine_folder.description:
The engine folder, as the host set it with the --engine-folder
command-line argument. The engine keeps its packages and logs there.

engine_version.description:
The engine release, as a date tag (yyyy-mm-dd, or yyyy-mm-dd-N for a
later release on the same day). Compare versions by date.

log_file.description:
The log file this engine process writes, in the logs subfolder of the
engine folder. Useful when reporting a problem.

packages.description: Every package in the engine's manifest, with its status.

platform.description: The platform the engine runs on, such as darwin-arm64.

protocol_versions.description: The MCP protocol versions the engine accepts, newest first.

outputSchema.title: GetEngineInfoOutput

name: install_packages
description: Installs or repairs the engine's toolchain packages, downloading them from the internet. Packages that are already installed and intact are left alone, unless force is set to download and install them again. Other tools install the packages they need on their own, so call this only to install ahead of time, such as before going offline, or when a tool returns a setup error with the install_packages action (for example when the engine was launched with automatic install turned off). A download can take a few minutes; the tool reports progress and can be cancelled.

inputSchema.description: Which packages to install or repair.

force.description:
Download and install the packages again even if they are installed,
replacing the installed copies. Use it when a package's tools fail in
ways that suggest damaged files. Defaults to false. Don't use it while
other operations are running.

packages.description:
Names of the packages to install or repair, as get_engine_info lists
them, such as oss-cad-suite. Omitted means every package in the
engine's manifest.

inputSchema.title: InstallPackagesInput

PackageInfo.description: A toolchain package and whether it's installed.

bin_folder.description:
The folder with the package's programs, as an absolute path, when
the package is installed. For hosts that run one of its programs
directly, such as Verible's language server verible-verilog-ls from
the verible package. Omitted when the package isn't installed.

name.description: The package name, such as oss-cad-suite.

version.description: The package release, as a date tag (yyyy-mm-dd).

PackageStatus.description: Whether a package is ready to use.

oneOf.description:
Installed but incomplete or damaged. It is repaired when a tool needs
it, unless auto-install is off.

outputSchema.description: What was installed, and every package's status afterwards.

installed.description:
Names of the packages this call installed, repaired or reinstalled.
Empty when they were all installed already and force was off.

packages.description: Every package in the engine's manifest, with its status.

outputSchema.title: InstallPackagesOutput

name: get_catalog
description: Returns board and FPGA definitions from the engine's read-only catalog. Use it to find a board's catalog ID, such as alhambra-ii, to pass as the board of other tools, or to see a board's FPGA and how it is programmed. Each section is returned only when asked for: {"boards": {"fetch": true}} returns all boards, and {"boards": {"fetch": true, "ids": ["alhambra-ii"]}} only the listed ones. Board descriptions are the boards' names for people.

CatalogQuery.description: Selects entries from one catalog section.

fetch.description: Whether to return this section. Defaults to false.

ids.description:
Catalog IDs of the entries to return. Omitted means all entries. An
ID that isn't in the section is an error.

boards.description: Which boards to return. Omitted means none.

fpgas.description: Which FPGAs to return. Omitted means none.

BoardDefinition.description:
A board: its FPGA and its variants. A board is a name: two boards with
different names are unrelated, even when their hardware is identical, as
are the sizes of a board sold with several FPGA sizes.

description.description: The board's name for people, such as "Alhambra II".

fpga_id.description:
The board's FPGA, as a catalog ID of the fpgas section, such as
ice40hx4k-tq144-8k. Every configuration uses it.

variants.description:
The board's choices, such as the cable or the memory to program, and
how to program it with each combination that exists.

Configuration.description:
One combination of the board's dimension values, and how to program the
board with it.

args.description:
The programmer's arguments, as a template. The engine replaces
${VID}, ${PID}, ${BUS} and ${DEV} with the device's USB vendor ID,
product ID, bus and device number, ${SERIAL} with its serial number,
and ${BITSTREAM} with the bitstream path.

programmer.description: The programmer to run: openfpgaloader, iceprog, dfu-util or icesprog.

tested.description:
Whether programming this way is known to work: tested on the board,
or used unchanged in a tool that relies on it. False for ways that
haven't been tried on hardware, such as a board moved to a different
programmer.

usb.description: The USB filter that finds the board's device.

user_notes.description:
Warnings and missing information for users, such as a USB filter that
also matches other boards or a step needed before programming.

when.description:
The value of every dimension, by dimension ID, such as
{"memory": "ram"}. Omitted or empty for a board without dimensions.

Dimension.description: One kind of choice, such as the memory to program.

id.description:
The dimension's ID, used in configurations and variant inputs, such as
connection or memory.

label.description: The dimension's name for people, such as "Connection".

values.description: The possible values, in the order to show them.

DimensionValue.description: One value of a dimension, such as RAM.

help.description:
A short explanation for people, such as "Faster to upload; lost when
the board is powered off."

id.description: The value's ID, such as ram.

label.description: The value's name for people, such as "RAM".

FpgaDefinition.description: An FPGA: its architecture, part and toolchain parameters.

architecture.description: The FPGA family: ice40, ecp5, gowin or xilinx.

nextpnr_device.description:
The device nextpnr uses, such as hx8k for iCE40, 25k for ECP5,
GW1NR-LV9QN88PC6/I5 for Gowin or xc7a35tcsg324-1 for Xilinx.

nextpnr_family.description:
The device family nextpnr uses, such as GW1N-9C, when nextpnr can't
tell it from nextpnr_device. Gowin only, optional.

nextpnr_package.description:
The package nextpnr uses, such as tq144:4k for iCE40 or CABGA256 for
ECP5. Required for iCE40 and ECP5; Gowin and Xilinx have none,
since their nextpnr_device names the package.

nextpnr_speed.description:
The speed grade nextpnr uses, such as 6. ECP5 only, where it's
required.

packer_device.description:
The device the bitstream packer (gowin_pack) uses, such as GW1N-9C.
Gowin only, where it's required.

part_number.description: The vendor's part number, such as ICE40HX4K-TQ144.

prjxray_family.description:
The FPGA family's folder in the Project X-Ray database, which the
bitstream tools read, such as artix7, spartan7 or zynq7. Xilinx
only, where it's required.

yosys_arch.description:
The architecture yosys synthesizes for (synth_xilinx -arch), such
as xc7. Xilinx only, where it's required.

yosys_family.description:
The family yosys synthesizes for, such as gw2a. Gowin only,
optional: omitted means yosys's default, the GW1N family.

UsbFilter.description: Which USB devices are this board.

pid.description: USB product ID, four lowercase hex digits, such as 6010.

product_regex.description:
A regular expression the device's product name must match, when
several boards share the same USB IDs. Omitted means any product name.

serial_regex.description:
A regular expression the device's serial number must match, for
boards that share USB IDs and product names but have serial numbers
that tell them apart. Omitted means any serial number.

vid.description: USB vendor ID, four lowercase hex digits, such as 0403.

Variants.description:
A board's choices (dimensions) and the combinations that exist
(configurations). They differ only in how the board is programmed: every
configuration has the same FPGA and pin file, so the same project works.
Every board has the two standard dimensions, connection and memory
(`STANDARD_DIMENSIONS`), whose values and their meanings the engine
defines; hosts decide how to show them (e.g. a choice only where a
dimension has more than one value).

configurations.description:
The combinations that exist, each with how to program the board. The
first is the board's default. Combinations that aren't listed don't
exist.

dimensions.description:
The standard dimensions, connection then memory, each with the values
the board's configurations use, with labels and help from the
engine. Derived from the configurations: ignored in inputs and not
written in the catalog file.

outputSchema.description: The requested catalog entries. Sections that weren't fetched are empty.
outputSchema.title: GetCatalogOutput

name: lint
description: Checks Verilog and SystemVerilog sources for errors and likely mistakes with Verilator, without building, like apio lint. It is much faster than build and finds problems synthesis accepts, such as width mismatches. List the design files and, optionally, the testbenches; the engine doesn't search for them. The board selects the FPGA's primitive models, so designs that use them lint cleanly. Problems found are the result, not an error: passed is false and diagnostics lists each problem at file and line, with Verilator's warning code at the end of the text, which a /* verilator lint_off CODE */ comment can silence. The first call may install the toolchain package first, which takes a few minutes. Writes nothing.

name: test
description: Runs testbenches with Icarus Verilog, like apio test: compiles the design files with each testbench, runs it, and reports whether it passed. A testbench fails by calling $fatal or $error, or by printing a failure line from Apio's assertion macros (*** ASSERTION FAILED or ERROR at file:line); it must end with $finish, and must not call $dumpfile, since the engine sets where its waveform goes (call $dumpvars to write one). Every listed testbench runs, even after one fails; each stops at its first failure unless stop_at_first_failure is false. A failing testbench is the result, not an error: passed is false, and each testbench's diagnostics and output say why. Compile errors are a design error with diagnostics at file and line. The first call may install the toolchain package first, which takes a few minutes. To look at a testbench's signals in a waveform viewer, use simulate.

name: simulate
description: Simulates one testbench with Icarus Verilog and opens its waveform in GTKWave, like apio sim: compiles the design files with the testbench, runs it to write the waveform (.vcd) into the build folder, then starts GTKWave detached and returns without waiting for it. The testbench must call $dumpvars and $finish, and must not call $dumpfile. GTKWave opens the layout file (.gtkw), which holds the signals shown; when it is missing, or is still a default one, the engine writes a default with the testbench's top-level signals, deleted again when GTKWave exits unless the user saved it; a layout the user saved is kept. Set open_viewer to false to only write the waveform, such as when no one is at the screen. A failing testbench runs to the end and is shown, with passed false and GTKWave's marker at the first failure in a default layout. Compile errors are a design error with diagnostics at file and line. To just check whether testbenches pass, use test.

Variants.description:
A board's choices (dimensions) and the combinations that exist
(configurations). They differ only in how the board is programmed: every
configuration has the same FPGA and pin file, so the same project works.
Every board has the two standard dimensions, connection and memory
(`STANDARD_DIMENSIONS`), whose values and their meanings the engine
defines; hosts decide how to show them (e.g. a choice only where a
dimension has more than one value).

configurations.description:
The combinations that exist, each with how to program the board. The
first is the board's default. Combinations that aren't listed don't
exist.

the board's configurations use, with labels and help from the
engine. Derived from the configurations: ignored in inputs and not
written in the catalog file.

inputSchema.description: Which testbench to simulate, and how to show it.

board.description:
The target board: a catalog ID such as alhambra-ii (get_catalog lists
them), or a full board definition. It selects the FPGA's primitive
models, such as SB_IO for iCE40, EHXPLLL for ECP5, rPLL for Gowin or PLLE2_BASE
for Xilinx.

build_folder.description:
Where the compiled testbench and its waveform go, as an absolute path.
One of its last two folder names must contain "build", such as

defines.description:
Verilog macro definitions, from name to value, such as

layout_file.description:
The GTKWave layout file (.gtkw), relative to the source folder, such
as main_tb.gtkw. GTKWave opens it and saves the user's changes to it.
When it is missing or is still a default one, the engine writes a
default there; a layout the user saved is never changed. Its folder
must exist. When omitted, the layout goes into the build folder, as
<testbench>.gtkw.

max_sim_time_ns.description:
Stop the testbench when simulated time reaches this many nanoseconds,
such as one that never calls $finish. Defaults to no limit.

open_viewer.description:
Open the waveform in GTKWave. Defaults to true. False only writes the
waveform and the layout.

source_files.description:
The design files (.v or .sv), relative to the source folder, with / as
the separator, such as ["main.v", "rtl/uart.v"]. Don't list
testbenches or included files.

source_folder.description:
The folder with the design files, as an absolute path. The testbench
runs in it, so it reads data files, such as with $readmemh, relative
to it.

testbench_file.description:
The testbench to simulate, relative to the source folder, such as
main_tb.v.

timeout_seconds.description:
Stop the testbench after this many seconds of real time, such as one
stuck in a loop. Defaults to no limit.

variant.description:
The board's variant, such as {"size": "85k"} or {"memory": "ram"}:
values of the board's dimensions, which get_catalog lists with the
configurations that exist. The first configuration with these values
is used; omitted dimensions match any value. Omitted means the
board's first configuration.

verbose.description:
Let iverilog print more detail, shown in the live output and the
logs. It doesn't change the result. Defaults to false.

name: format
description: Formats Verilog and SystemVerilog files in place with Verible's formatter, like apio format. List the files to format (.v, .sv, .vh or .svh); the engine doesn't search for them. Formatting changes only layout, never meaning. Each file is rewritten only when its layout changes; files lists each one as formatted, unchanged or failed. A file Verible can't parse, such as one with a syntax error, is left unchanged: passed is false and diagnostics gives the error at file and line. That is a result, not an error. Code between // verilog_format: off and // verilog_format: on comments is left as is. The first call may install the Verible package first.

name: graph
description: Draws a diagram of a design module, its cells, ports and the wires between them, like apio graph --no-viewer: yosys reads the design without synthesizing it and Graphviz draws the module. Writes graph.svg (or .pdf or .png) and Graphviz's graph.dot in the build folder, replacing the last ones; graph_file gives its path relative to the build folder. List the design files; the engine doesn't search for them. Errors in the design, such as a syntax error or a top module that isn't in the files, are design errors with diagnostics at file and line. The first call may install the toolchain package first, which takes a few minutes.

name: build
description: Builds an FPGA design into a bitstream: synthesizes the Verilog or SystemVerilog sources, places and routes them on the board's FPGA using the constraint file, which maps top-level ports to pins (.pcf for iCE40, .lpf for ECP5, .cst for Gowin, .xdc for Xilinx), and packs the bitstream into the build folder. Give the source files explicitly; the engine doesn't search for them, though `include files are found next to the including file or in the source folder. A build with no changes since the last one returns at once with up_to_date set. The first build may install the toolchain package first, which takes a few minutes. Design problems come back as a design error with diagnostics at file and line. After a successful build, program_board programs the bitstream into the board.

resources_usage.description:
Resource use, by the toolchain's resource name, such as ICESTORM_LC
(logic cells: a LUT and a flip-flop), ICESTORM_RAM (block RAMs) and
SB_IO (I/O pins).

timing.description:
The maximum frequency each clock can run at, in MHz, by clock net
name. A clock that misses its target isn't an error: compare these
with the design's needs.

up_to_date.description:
True if nothing had changed since the last build, so nothing was
rebuilt.

name: clean_build
description: Deletes build folders, like apio clean. Given a build folder, such as /home/u/proj/_build/default, it deletes it. Given a folder of build folders, such as /home/u/proj/_build, it deletes each build folder directly inside it, then the folder itself if nothing else is left. It only deletes folders the build tool made, so other files are never removed. A folder that doesn't exist is fine.

folder.description:
A build folder, or a folder whose direct subfolders are build
folders, as an absolute path. One of its last two folder names must
contain "build".

deleted.description:
The deleted folders, as absolute paths, including the given folder
when it was deleted. Empty when there was nothing to delete.

name: list_devices
description: Lists the USB devices connected to this computer, with their USB IDs, names and serial numbers, and for each the boards it may be: catalog boards, and the request's custom_boards, each with a confidence (named: the device's name matched the board's; chip: only its USB chip did) and the variants it fits. program_board needs the id of one of these devices: pick the device whose boards include the build's board. Devices that need a driver or permissions first are listed apart, under unreachable, with the fix.

BoardInputDefinition.description:
A board definition in a request. Like a catalog entry, except that the
FPGA can be given either as fpga_id or as a full fpga definition.

fpga.description: The board's FPGA as a full definition. Give either fpga_id or fpga.

fpga_id.description:
The board's FPGA as a catalog ID, such as ice40hx4k-tq144-8k. Give
either fpga_id or fpga.

variants.description:
The board's choices and how to program it with each, as in the
catalog.

Configuration.description:
One combination of the board's dimension values, and how to program the
board with it.

args.description:
The programmer's arguments, as a template. The engine replaces
${VID}, ${PID}, ${BUS} and ${DEV} with the device's USB vendor ID,
product ID, bus and device number, ${SERIAL} with its serial number,
and ${BITSTREAM} with the bitstream path.

programmer.description: The programmer to run: openfpgaloader, iceprog, dfu-util or icesprog.

tested.description:
Whether programming this way is known to work: tested on the board,
or used unchanged in a tool that relies on it. False for ways that
haven't been tried on hardware, such as a board moved to a different
programmer.

usb.description: The USB filter that finds the board's device.

user_notes.description:
Warnings and missing information for users, such as a USB filter that
also matches other boards or a step needed before programming.

when.description:
The value of every dimension, by dimension ID, such as
{"memory": "ram"}. Omitted or empty for a board without dimensions.

Dimension.description: One kind of choice, such as the memory to program.

id.description:
The dimension's ID, used in configurations and variant inputs, such as
connection or memory.

label.description: The dimension's name for people, such as "Connection".

values.description: The possible values, in the order to show them.

DimensionValue.description: One value of a dimension, such as RAM.

help.description:
A short explanation for people, such as "Faster to upload; lost when
the board is powered off."

id.description: The value's ID, such as ram.

label.description: The value's name for people, such as "RAM".

FpgaDefinition.description: An FPGA: its architecture, part and toolchain parameters.

architecture.description: The FPGA family: ice40, ecp5, gowin or xilinx.

nextpnr_device.description:
The device nextpnr uses, such as hx8k for iCE40, 25k for ECP5,
GW1NR-LV9QN88PC6/I5 for Gowin or xc7a35tcsg324-1 for Xilinx.

nextpnr_family.description:
The device family nextpnr uses, such as GW1N-9C, when nextpnr can't
tell it from nextpnr_device. Gowin only, optional.

nextpnr_package.description:
The package nextpnr uses, such as tq144:4k for iCE40 or CABGA256 for
ECP5. Required for iCE40 and ECP5; Gowin and Xilinx have none,
since their nextpnr_device names the package.

nextpnr_speed.description:
The speed grade nextpnr uses, such as 6. ECP5 only, where it's
required.

packer_device.description:
The device the bitstream packer (gowin_pack) uses, such as GW1N-9C.
Gowin only, where it's required.

part_number.description: The vendor's part number, such as ICE40HX4K-TQ144.

prjxray_family.description:
The FPGA family's folder in the Project X-Ray database, which the
bitstream tools read, such as artix7, spartan7 or zynq7. Xilinx
only, where it's required.

yosys_arch.description:
The architecture yosys synthesizes for (synth_xilinx -arch), such
as xc7. Xilinx only, where it's required.

yosys_family.description:
The family yosys synthesizes for, such as gw2a. Gowin only,
optional: omitted means yosys's default, the GW1N family.

UsbFilter.description: Which USB devices are this board.

pid.description: USB product ID, four lowercase hex digits, such as 6010.

product_regex.description:
A regular expression the device's product name must match, when
several boards share the same USB IDs. Omitted means any product name.

serial_regex.description:
A regular expression the device's serial number must match, for
boards that share USB IDs and product names but have serial numbers
that tell them apart. Omitted means any serial number.

vid.description: USB vendor ID, four lowercase hex digits, such as 0403.

Variants.description:
A board's choices (dimensions) and the combinations that exist
(configurations). They differ only in how the board is programmed: every
configuration has the same FPGA and pin file, so the same project works.
Every board has the two standard dimensions, connection and memory
(`STANDARD_DIMENSIONS`), whose values and their meanings the engine
defines; hosts decide how to show them (e.g. a choice only where a
dimension has more than one value).

configurations.description:
The combinations that exist, each with how to program the board. The
first is the board's default. Combinations that aren't listed don't
exist.

dimensions.description:
The standard dimensions, connection then memory, each with the values
the board's configurations use, with labels and help from the
engine. Derived from the configurations: ignored in inputs and not
written in the catalog file.

inputSchema.description:
Optionally, the host's own boards to match the devices against, besides
the catalog's.

custom_boards.description:
The host's own board definitions, by board ID (lowercase letters,
digits and hyphens), in the same format as the board field of other
tools. Devices are matched against them as well as the catalog's
boards; matches name them with custom true. Omitted means none.

inputSchema.title: ListDevicesInput

Action.description: A suggested action, with a code for the host and a description for people.

ActionCode.description: A fix the host can offer the user.

oneOf.description:
Required packages are missing or broken and weren't installed
automatically, because auto-install is off or the install failed.
A device was found but cannot be opened.
A driver required by the board is missing.

Other connected devices have the board's USB IDs, and the board's
programmer can't tell them apart. Disconnect them and retry.

BoardMatch.description: A board a device may be.

board.description:
The board's ID: a catalog ID, or a key of the request's
custom_boards when custom is true.

confidence.description:
How sure the match is. named: the device's product name or serial
number matched the board's pattern, so the device says it is this
kind of board (several boards can still share one name). chip: only
the USB IDs matched, so it is any device with this USB chip, often
many boards and adapters.

custom.description:
True when the board is one of the request's custom_boards rather
than the catalog's. A custom board can have a catalog board's ID; the
host decides which one it means.

variants.description:
The board's variants this device fits, as dimension values, such as
{"connection": "usb", "memory": "flash"}, in the board's order.

oneOf.description: The device's name or serial number matched the board's pattern.

Device.description: A connected device that the engine can open.

boards.description:
The boards whose USB filters this device matches, best first. Empty
for a device that is no known board.

device.description:
USB device number on its bus. It changes when the device is plugged
in again.

id.description:
The device's ID, to pass to program_board. Opaque: don't parse it.
It names the device on this computer for a short time: it stays
valid while the device stays on the same USB port, so list the
devices again before asking the user to choose.

manufacturer.description: The manufacturer name the device reports, when available.

pid.description: USB product ID, four lowercase hex digits.

product.description: The product name the device reports, when available.

serial_number.description: The serial number the device reports, when available.

vid.description: USB vendor ID, four lowercase hex digits.

UnreachableDevice.description:
A device the engine sees but can't open, so it can't read its names or
program it: it needs a driver or permissions first. Listed only when its
USB IDs fit a board.

action.description: What makes the device usable, such as fix_device_permissions.

boards.description:
The boards whose USB IDs it has. Their confidence is always chip,
since its names can't be read.

device.description: USB device number on its bus.

pid.description: USB product ID, four lowercase hex digits.

vid.description: USB vendor ID, four lowercase hex digits.

devices.description:
The connected USB devices the engine can open, sorted by vendor ID,
product ID, bus and device number.

unreachable.description:
Devices the engine sees but can't open, so it can't program them or
read their names, and whose USB IDs fit a board: each with the fix,
such as permissions or a driver. Other devices it can't open are left
out.

name: program_board
description: Programs the bitstream of a successful build into the board it was built for. It doesn't build: call build first, and program_board only if the build succeeded. The board comes from the build, so it takes the build folder and the device to program: the id of a device from list_devices whose boards include the build's board (ask the user when several do). A device that isn't connected anymore is a setup error with connect_board; list the devices again. Most boards are programmed to flash, so the design stays after power-off.

inputSchema.description: Which build to program, and into which device.

build_folder.description: The build folder of a successful build, as an absolute path.

device.description:
The device to program: the id of a device from list_devices, such as
one whose boards include the build's board. It must still be
connected and match the board's USB filter.

programmer_command.description:
A custom programmer command that replaces the board's default one,
like Apio's programmer_cmd. Its first word is a program from the
toolchain package, such as openFPGALoader, or an absolute path. It may
use ${VID}, ${PID}, ${BUS}, ${DEV}, ${SERIAL} and must use
${BITSTREAM}.

verbose.description:
Let the programmer print more detail, shown in the live output and
the logs. Not applied to a programmer_command. Defaults to false.

inputSchema.title: ProgramBoardInput

BoardMatch.description: A board a device may be.

board.description:
The board's ID: a catalog ID, or a key of the request's
custom_boards when custom is true.

confidence.description:
How sure the match is. named: the device's product name or serial

variants.description:

CommandRecord.description: One program the engine ran, with what it takes to run it again.

args.description:
The program as an absolute path, then its arguments, exactly as
passed.

cwd.description: The folder it ran in, as an absolute path.

package.description:
The package the program came from, with its version, such as
"oss-cad-suite 2026-10-22". Omitted for a program from elsewhere, such
as a custom programmer command.

shell.description:
One shell command line that runs it again the same way: in the same
folder, with the same minimal environment (PATH, HOME and TMPDIR).

tool.description: The program's name, such as yosys.

oneOf.description: The device's name or serial number matched the board's pattern.

Device.description: A connected device that the engine can open.

boards.description:
The boards whose USB filters this device matches, best first. Empty
for a device that is no known board.

device.description:
USB device number on its bus. It changes when the device is plugged
in again.

id.description:
The device's ID, to pass to program_board. Opaque: don't parse it.
It names the device on this computer for a short time: it stays
valid while the device stays on the same USB port, so list the

manufacturer.description: The manufacturer name the device reports, when available.

pid.description: USB product ID, four lowercase hex digits.

product.description: The product name the device reports, when available.

serial_number.description: The serial number the device reports, when available.

vid.description: USB vendor ID, four lowercase hex digits.

commands.description:
The programs this call ran, in order, each with the exact command and
a shell line that runs it again without the engine, such as for a bug
report to the tool's developers.

programmer.description:
The programmer that was used, such as openfpgaloader, or custom for a
programmer_command.
